findings: An infiltrative pancreatic cancer measuring 51 mm is observed in the body of the pancreas. Serosal invasion and retropancreatic tissue invasion are noted. There is contact of more than 180° with the superior mesenteric vein, suggesting invasion. No invasion beyond the inferior border of the duodenum is observed. Contact of more than 180° with the splenic artery is also observed, indicating possible invasion. No other local invasion factors are identified. No lymph node metastases are present. A hypodense mass is observed in the left lobe of the liver, raising suspicion of liver metastasis.
